p1Closed.finding: #1 engine-protocol 2.2/2.4/4: an account's single switchThreshold has no place in the two menus, so Default/null for one window cannot reach the global default
p1Closed.note: Section 2.1 says: "Splitting the single value. Before any per-window write (a Session or Weekly menu choice other than Manual only, Default included; accounts.setThresholds with a number or null; CLI --session/--weekly), if the account's switchThreshold is 1-100, copy it into each of sessionThreshold/weeklyThreshold that is nil, set switchThreshold to nil, then apply the write. So Default / null / default always means the global window default. (Test and vector: switchThreshold 70, Session set to Default: session = defaults.session, weekly = 70, switchThreshold = nil.)" Section 2.4 adds the label rule ("Switch at N%" when the account has its own value for that window, else "Default (N%)"), and section 4 says setThresholds "Applies the 2.1 split and Manual only rules". Small gap: the label rule names only the session pair (sessionThreshold ?? switchThreshold). The weekly one (weeklyThreshold ?? switchThreshold) is implied, not written.

p1Closed.finding: #2 engine-protocol 2.3/AppState: the verification, noteStayingPut and the log lines still use one threshold, so ranking and verification can disagree
p1Closed.note: Rule 10 says: "AppState (and the Linux coordinator) call only the two-window entry points ... The fresh-reading verification before a switch (AppState.swift:1230-1236) checks the TARGET's resolved pair with the same eligibility function, in the mode (strict or relaxed) the plan was made in. noteStayingPut (:1279-1291) and the decision log lines (:1200-1207, 1241-1243) use the active account's leaveAt pair and name the window. AutoSwitchRecord gains window." Rule 8 adds "no non-test file may call them (a grep in section 7 acceptance proves it)", and section 7 repeats the grep. I checked every cited AppState line range against the current file and they are correct.

p1Closed.finding: #3 engine-protocol 2.1/2.2: an absent global window key read with double(forKey:) as 0 would drop every default to 50

(Test: with only autoSwitchThreshold = 98 stored, both effective defaults read 98 and settings.get returns 98 for both new keys.)"

p1Closed.finding: #4 engine-protocol 4: setPriority inherited recon's 1...count position range and a required MCP argument, so null could never clear a priority
p1Closed.note: Section 4 says: "Recon 4.3's position-based setPriority (range 1...count, AccountOrder.moved) does NOT apply". p1Closed.finding: #5 engine-protocol: priority shown as '#n' reads as the position column
p1Closed.note: Section 3 says: "A priority number is never an account reference. References stay id, email, label and position ... Priorities are shown as P1 everywhere so they cannot be read as #1." p1Closed.finding: #6 linux-safety 5.3: a refresh lock taken only around the write still loses the leaving account's rotated token
p1Closed.note: Section 5.3 says: "take it BEFORE step 4's final read of the live credential, hold it through the merge read (step 5), the write and the read-back (step 6), release it in a finally ... Wait at most 35 s ... Hold it at most 10 s, keep it touched ... never remove, break or take over a lock PixelSwitch did not create. If it cannot be confirmed: take no lock and say so in the README." It also adds "Re-read before write (both platforms, always, lock or not) ... Unit-test the compare." This is the reviewer's fix in full.

p1Closed.finding: #7 linux-safety D12: the blank-login guard covered saving only and had type holes
p1Closed.note: D12 is rewritten word for word from the fix: "usable login only if it parses as a JSON object whose claudeAiOauth is an object with accessToken a non-empty string, refreshToken a non-empty string, and expiresAt (when present) a number greater than 0 ... (a) is never saved, enforced inside the one store-save function ... (b) is never written to Claude Code's live store: target validation fails with the re-sign message instead of passing; (c) makes the account not switchable". The problem can no longer happen if this is built as written. One gap: the reviewer's test list (blank tokens, missing claudeAiOauth, null fields, expiresAt 0, each tested against save, switch and isSwitchable) was not carried over. Adding it to the section 7 acceptance would pin the rule.

p1Closed.finding: #8 linux-safety 5.3: renewal never updates refreshTokenExpiresAt
p1Closed.note: Section 5.3 says: "Renewal keeps refreshTokenExpiresAt honest (both platforms): on success, if the response has a positive refresh_token_expires_in, set claudeAiOauth.refreshTokenExpiresAt = now_ms + refresh_token_expires_in * 1000; if it has none and the stored value is in the past, remove the key ... Unit tests for both cases."

p1Closed.finding: #9 linux-safety 5.4/5.1: the updater restart ignored an in-flight renewal, and SIGTERM had no handling
p1Closed.note: Section 5.4 says: "Restart only when no switch, sign-in, saved-login renewal or store write is in progress." Section 5.1 says: "On SIGTERM or SIGINT it starts no new cycle, switch, renewal or sign-in, lets in-flight renewals finish their POST, ownership check and save (bounded by the request timeouts, at most 80 s), cancels a running sign-in as Cancel does, then exits 0." The unit sets "KillMode=mixed, TimeoutStopSec=90", and 80 s fits inside 90 s.

p1Closed.finding: #10 linux-safety 5.1: no Restart policy or start limit
p1Closed.note: Section 5.1 says: "Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=120, StartLimitIntervalSec=3600, StartLimitBurst=4 ... An automatic restart is the only thing that limits how often the unpersisted guard state is lost, so nothing restarts the daemon in a loop. (A test checks the unit file holds these.)" The spec text is closed, but it does not say which unit-file section the start-limit keys go in. Placed in [Service], the limit silently does nothing. See new P2 'systemd start-limit keys'.

p1Closed.finding: #11 linux-safety 5.2: XDG-dependent socket allowed a second daemon
p1Closed.note: Section 5.1 says: "Takes an exclusive fcntl.flock on ~/.local/state/pixelswitch/daemon.lock (path from HOME only) before reading any store or binding the socket, for its whole life; if held, it exits 0 with 'already running' and touches nothing. Only while holding it may it unlink a stale socket. It writes the socket path it bound to ~/.local/state/pixelswitch/socket-path." Also "They never exec pixelswitchd; they start it only with systemctl --user start pixelswitch.service", and section 5.2 says "Clients read socket-path first". See new P2 'self-check vs lock' for a side effect of this rule.

p1Closed.finding: #12 linux-safety 5.2: only login files had to be atomic/0600; ~/.claude.json and others could become world-readable
p1Closed.note: Section 5.2 says: "Every file PixelSwitch writes (.credentials.json, ~/.claude.json, backups.json, settings.json, accounts.json, state files) is written atomically: a temp file in the target's directory opened O_CREAT|O_EXCL at 0600, written, fsync'd, os.replace'd, then the directory fsync'd ... A symlinked or hard-linked target is refused. Directories PixelSwitch creates are 0700. The log is opened 0600." Section 5.1 adds os.umask(0o077), and the unit sets UMask=0077.

p1Closed.finding: #13 linux-safety 5.4: an unsigned feed allowed a downgrade and unchecked paths
p1Closed.note: Section 5.4 says: "Nothing in the feed is trusted until checked: version is two whole numbers joined by a dot; build a whole number greater than the running build; url starts with https://github.com/BespokeWoodcraftStudio/PixelSwitch/releases/download/v<version>/; size at most 50 MB, and the download is cut off at size. Size, SHA-256 and signature are checked BEFORE anything is extracted ... tarfile filter='data'. The tarball carries a VERSION file ... that must equal the feed's". p1Closed.finding: #14 linux-safety 5.4: no self-check or rollback, so a broken build bricks updates
p1Closed.note: Section 5.4 says: "python3 -I <new>/bin/pixelswitchd --self-check ... Flip current only on exit 0 with a matching version ... Keep the previous version's directory ... A small stdlib ExecStartPre script installed outside the versioned directories flips current back to the previous version when the current build has failed to start 3 times without writing its good marker." The tests include "a self-check failure, the rollback". Two new P2s cover how this meets the 5.1 lock and the start limit.

p1Closed.finding: #15 linux-safety 5.6: signing in the every-run linux-package job exposed SPARKLE_EDDSA_KEY

p1Closed.finding: #17 scope 2.3: the founder's own 90/50 example stops auto-switch even at 100% of a session
p1Closed.note: Mostly adopted: D19 and card C4, rule 9, the 2.4 sentence ("When every account is past its weekly limit, the session limit decides.") and the section 6 vectors. The exact case the finding names, every account including the active one past 49%, is fixed. The same harm is still there, though. Rule 9 requires "active: w >= leaveAt.weekly" and every usable candidate to have a known weekly reading past its weekly limit. So when the active account reaches its session limit while still under its own weekly limit (typically the account whose week just reset), the user sits at 100% of a session for up to 5 hours while the other accounts have session room and 50-89% of their week used. Example: X at session 90, weekly 18; the others at weekly 64 and 72. The same happens when one candidate is under its weekly limit but has no session room, or has no weekly reading. That is the sentence the finding complains about. The fix is new finding 1.

p1Closed.finding: #18 scope 2.3 rule 5: a low weekly threshold quietly cancels use-it-before-it-resets drains
p1Closed.note: Closed in a different way, and I checked the reason. D19 says "outside overflow that would ping-pong (the drain lands on an account past its weekly limit, rule 1 moves you back after the cooldown), so drains follow the weekly limit until overflow holds, and in overflow they use the raised limit". Proof: A at session 40, weekly 30; B at session 10, weekly 70, resetting in 10 h. A drain that ignored the weekly limit would move A to B. After 300 s, rule 1 on B (70 >= 50) finds A eligible (40 <= 89, 30 <= 49) and moves back to A. Then the drain fires again: a switch, and a login rewrite, every 300 s. So the reviewer's recommended option (a) was unsafe, and revision 2's rule is the only one that does not oscillate without changing rule 1. The decision is no longer silent: D19 records it. His literal example (95% used) is not a drain target at a 90 threshold in 1.9 either (ceiling 89). Polish: card C4 should say this in one sentence so he is told, not only the spec.

p1Closed.finding: #19 scope 2.2/2.4/4: same problem as #1 (Default lands on the legacy 70, not the default)

newFindings.section: 2.3 rule 9 (weekly overflow, D19), 2.4 General sentence, 6 vectors
newFindings.problem: The overflow test is too narrow. It still leaves the user at 100% of a session, the harm D19 exists to remove, and none of its extra conditions prevents a ping-pong. (1) It requires the active account to be past its own weekly limit. When the active account reaches its session limit while still under its weekly limit, overflow fails and the user stays. Example: the founder's accounts pv at weekly 72, gmail at 64, X at 3 because its week just reset. Strict moves him to X. X reaches session 90 at weekly 18. Strict finds nothing (72 > 49, 64 > 49), overflow fails (18 < 50), and he sits on X through 100% of the session for up to 5 hours while pv and gmail have their whole session free. 1.9 at a 90 threshold would have moved him to gmail. This repeats every session of X's week until X passes 50%. (2) It requires every candidate to be past its weekly limit. A candidate under its weekly limit but with no session room blocks overflow for everyone. Example: pv at session 92, weekly 70; gmail at session 95, weekly 30; X at session 10, weekly 60: he stays on pv. Case (h) is the same: an account whose own weekly rule is above its session rule (session 70, weekly 95) is practically never past its weekly ceiling of 94. As a candidate it blocks overflow for every other account, and as the active account it never overflows (session 70, weekly 40). (3) It requires a known weekly reading on every candidate. A candidate with no weekly reading blocks overflow: its week reset since its last round-robin sample, it was never polled, or it is parked. Combined with a no-subscription active account, the user is left on an account that cannot be used at all. Why none of this buys safety: when strict is nil, every candidate with session room and a weekly reading is already past its weekly ceiling (otherwise rule 3 would have chosen it), and a candidate with no session room or no reading is not a target in either mode. The only real ping-pongs are a drain or a Fable-only trigger from an active account still under both window limits. Example: A at session 40, weekly 30; a drain moves to B at weekly 70; after 300 s rule 1 on B moves back to A; the drain fires again. Requiring that the active account has reached a strict window limit already rules those out. So the spec's parenthetical is right for drains and Fable but wrong for moves made at the session limit. Side cost: the candidate clause needs isSwitchable for each candidate, and every call is a Keychain read plus an info log line, on most cycles of a 90/50 week.
newFindings.evidence: Spec lines 124-132 ("Overflow holds when the active account (unless it has no subscription) and every candidate that is switchable, usable and not Manual only have a known weekly reading, and each is past its own strict weekly limit"). D19 line 55 ("so the session limit keeps moving you"; "Without it his own example (90 / 50) stops auto-switch ... even at 100% of a session"). Section 6 lines 417-418 pin "overflow does not hold because one account has no weekly reading". In the engine, the drain fires only when no threshold was reached (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:336-339). rankedTargets checks usage before isSwitchable because isSwitchable reads the Keychain (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:399-404, AppState.swift:1115-1121), and every lookup logs (KeychainService.swift:245-258). Round-robin polls the active account plus one other per cycle (recon usage.md:510). The cooldown is 300 s (AppState.swift:130, :1155) and every switch restarts it (:832, :1257).
newFindings.fix: Replace the overflow definition in rule 9 with: "Overflow holds when `strict` is nil and the active account has no subscription, or has reached its strict limit on the windows by rule 1 (`s >= leaveAt.session` or `w >= leaveAt.weekly`, under rule 1's expiry rule; a Fable-only trigger does not count). Nothing is required of the candidates." Replace the parenthetical with: "A relaxed plan is never made from an active account that is still under both its strict window limits: a drain or Fable move from it would land on an account past its weekly limit, and rule 1 would bring you back after the cooldown." Change the 2.4 sentence in all five string tables, and the card C4 text, to "When no account under its weekly limit can take you, the session limit decides." In section 6, change the 'no weekly reading' vector to expect a move, and add vectors that must move: active under its weekly limit at session 90; a candidate under its weekly limit with session 95; a candidate with no reading; a no-subscription active with such a candidate; a (70, 95) override as candidate and as active. Add vectors that must stay: a drain from an active under both limits; a Fable-only trigger from an active under both limits. Add a two-cycle vector showing no return within the cooldown. Proof that no ping-pong is possible: a relaxed move from A needs A at session >= its limit, weekly >= its limit, or no subscription. A becomes a strict target again only after the window that fired resets, because readings only grow within a window. It becomes a relaxed target only after X itself reaches a relaxed limit or A's session window resets. Drains need a strictly earlier weekly reset, so they cannot cycle. So a return always needs a window reset or real use of X, never just the 300 s cooldown.

newFindings.problem: While overflow holds, the active account sits past its strict weekly limit for days on purpose. noteStayingPut uses the strict leaveAt pair, so it logs "at 60% on weekly (its threshold 50%), but no other account has room under its own threshold; staying put" every time the percentage changes. That is false: other accounts do have room under the raised limit, and PixelSwitch is waiting for the session limit. The per-account help text "moves you to it only while it is at ... 49% or less of its week" is also wrong during overflow.
newFindings.evidence: Spec line 136 (noteStayingPut uses the active account's leaveAt pair) and line 155-157 (the help text). AppState.swift:1279-1296 logs once per change of a string that includes the percentage.
newFindings.fix: When overflow holds and the relaxed plan is nil, noteStayingPut logs once per change: "no account under its weekly limit can take you; staying until the session limit (N%)". When the windows differ, the help text adds "(up to S-1% of its week when no account under its weekly limit can take you)".

newFindings.section: 2.1 (Only a number clears Manual only) and 2.4 menus
newFindings.problem: Section 2.1 makes Default in a window menu a per-window null write, and "null (Default) on a Manual only account changes nothing". So on a Manual only row both menus read "Manual only" and choosing Default does nothing. In 1.9 the menu's Default took the account out of Manual only. In 2.0 the only way out in the GUI is to pick a number and then pick Default.
newFindings.evidence: Spec lines 71-78. SettingsAccountsTab.swift:161-163 (1.9's Default calls setSwitchThreshold(nil), which clears Manual only).
newFindings.fix: Add to 2.4: "In Settings, Default in either menu of a Manual only account clears Manual only and both windows follow their defaults (1.9's Default). accounts.setThresholds with null still leaves Manual only alone." Add a test.

newFindings.problem: Rule 8 names plan, rankedTargets, eligibleUtilization and drainEligibleUtilization as the entry points the tests call. The tests never call rankedTargets or drainEligibleUtilization. They do reference AutoSwitchSettings.leaveAtThreshold and .explanation without arguments, and they declare plan's result type as (limit, trigger, targets). If a two-window helper is added as an overload of either of those two names, those lines become ambiguous and the unchanged tests stop compiling. A compatibility plan that returns the new window or relaxed fields breaks them the same way.
newFindings.evidence: Tests/UnitTests/AutoSwitchRulesTests.swift:32 (typealias Plan = (limit:, trigger:, targets:)), :428 (let leave = AutoSwitchSettings.leaveAtThreshold), :459 (let e = AutoSwitchSettings.explanation); Tests/UnitTests/main.swift:320. A grep of Tests/ finds no rankedTargets or drainEligibleUtilization.
newFindings.fix: Add to rule 8: "The compatibility plan returns exactly (limit: Limit, trigger: Trigger, targets: [Account])?. Two-window helpers get new names and are never overloads of leaveAtThreshold or explanation, which the tests reference without arguments." Correct the list to the entry points the tests actually use.

newFindings.problem: The spec lists StartLimitIntervalSec=3600 and StartLimitBurst=4 but not their section. systemd reads both from [Unit] (systemd.unit(5)); [Service] accepts only the legacy StartLimitInterval=/StartLimitBurst= names. If both are written under [Service], StartLimitIntervalSec is ignored with a warning and the 10 s default applies. With RestartSec=120 the limit then never trips, and the restart loop finding #10 closed comes back. A test that only greps for the lines still passes.
newFindings.fix: Write: "[Unit] StartLimitIntervalSec=3600, StartLimitBurst=4; [Service] Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=120, KillMode=mixed, TimeoutStopSec=90, UMask=0077". The unit-file test checks the section of each key, and CI runs systemd-analyze --user verify on the file.

newFindings.problem: The start limit can block the rollback. The updater checks two minutes after start, so a laptop that was off at release time does this: boot start (1), update restart into the new build (2, fails), (3, fails), (4, fails). The ExecStartPre that would roll back runs only on start 5, after 3 failures, and StartLimitBurst=4 within 3600 s refuses start 5. The service stays failed, with every face's systemctl --user start refused, until the hour passes and some client happens to start it.
newFindings.evidence: Spec lines 248 (StartLimitBurst=4 per 3600 s), 314-315 (check two minutes after start), 329-332 (roll back after 3 failed starts).
newFindings.fix: Roll back after 2 failed starts of a build that has no good marker, and state the rule: boot start + update restart + failures + the rolled-back start must fit within StartLimitBurst. Unit-test the sequence boot, update, failures, rollback.

newFindings.problem: Section 5.1 says pixelswitchd takes the daemon lock "before reading any store" and, if the lock is held, "exits 0 with 'already running' and touches nothing". The self-check is `pixelswitchd --self-check`, run while the live daemon holds that lock. Read literally, it exits 0 without printing the version, the flip never happens, and no Linux client ever applies an update. None of the listed tests runs the self-check beside a running daemon, so this would first surface at 2.1.
newFindings.fix: Add to 5.4: "--self-check takes no lock, binds no socket and writes nothing (it reads the stores read-only, without the lock)". Add a unit test that runs the self-check while a test daemon holds the lock.

overflowAnalysis:
Notation for the 90/50 example. Strict: leave at session >= 90 or weekly >= 50; arrive only at session <= 89 and weekly <= 49 (ceiling(90,1) = 89, ceiling(50,1) = 49). Relaxed: weekly becomes max(50, 90) = 90, so leave at session >= 90 or weekly >= 90 and arrive at session <= 89 and weekly <= 89. The cooldown is 300 s (AppState.swift:130, :1155) and is restarted by every switch (:832, :1257); only a no-subscription active account skips it (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:226-229). Verification takes one fresh reading per evaluation and uses the same eligibility rule, in the plan's mode (AppState.swift:1212-1245, rule 10). Below, s, w and f are an account's session, weekly and Fable use.

(a) Beeco Mac, 98 everywhere. Only autoSwitchThreshold = 98 is stored, so under 2.1's presence rule the defaults are (98, 98), and every account's rule is (98, 98) or (t, t) from its switchThreshold. max(w, s) = w for every account and for the defaults, so the relaxed plan gets exactly the strict plan's inputs. Since plan is a pure function, relaxed == strict and strict ?? relaxed == strict: the overflow test can add a computation but can never change a result. Strict is also 1.9's plan. With equal pairs, rule 1 becomes max(s, w) >= 98; rule 3 becomes every known reading <= 97; rule 6 becomes room = 98 - max(s, w); the drain uses ceiling(98, 1) = 97 on both windows and Fable; Fable uses f >= 98 and f <= 97. Example: A at s 98 / w 40, B at 20/97, C at 5/99. Both 1.9 and 2.0 pick B; if B were at w 98, both stay. This still holds under the proposed fix.

(b) Three accounts on 90/50, Most room left.
Trace 1, overflow holds. A is active at s 92 / w 62, B at 15/58, C at 40/75. Strict: A fires on session; B (58 > 49) and C (75 > 49) do not qualify, so strict is nil. Overflow: A 62 >= 50, B 58 > 49, C 75 > 49, so it holds. Relaxed: B's room is min(75, 32) = 32 and C's is min(50, 15) = 15, so PixelSwitch switches to B (verified in relaxed mode). 300 s later on B (20/59): strict fires (59 >= 50), but A's session 92 is above 89 and C's weekly is above 49, so strict is nil. Overflow still holds, and under relaxed B is at neither 90 limit, so it stays every cycle until B reaches session 90 or weekly 90. At B session 90 (weekly 70) it moves to A if A's session window has reset (room min(90, 28) = 28), otherwise to C (room 15). B can be a target again only after its session resets. No 300 s return is possible: you leave only at 90 or above, arrive only at 89 or below, and readings only grow inside a window.
Trace 2, stranded under rule 9 as written. pv is at weekly 72, gmail at 64, X at 3 (its week just reset). Strict moves pv to X. X reaches session 90 at weekly 18. Strict is nil, and overflow fails on the active clause (18 < 50), so he stays through 100% of X's session for up to 5 hours while pv and gmail are near session 0. 1.9 at 90 would move him to gmail. Under the fix: relaxed picks gmail (room 26 against pv's 18). 300 s later strict fires on gmail (64 >= 50), X (session 90 or more) and pv (72 > 49) do not qualify, so strict is nil; overflow holds because gmail is at its weekly limit; relaxed has no trigger, so it stays. When X's session window resets, X (weekly 18) is a strict target and he moves gmail to X; when X reaches session 90 again, relaxed moves him to gmail or pv. The cycle period is X's session length, never 300 s.
Trace 2b, stranded as written. pv at 92/70, gmail at 95/30, X at 10/60: gmail (30 <= 49) blocks overflow. The fix moves him to X; when gmail's session resets, strict moves him X to gmail.
Guarantee: with the fix he is left at a session limit only when every other usable account with session room is above the raised weekly ceiling (89). That is 1.9's behaviour at a 90 threshold since 1.8 removed the exhausted rule. Neither D19 nor 1.9 promises 'any weekly below 100'.

(c) Drain (Resets soonest, drain on, 24 h window). Without overflow: A at 40/30, B at 10/45 resetting in 6 h, so the strict drain moves him to B. From B, another drain needs an even earlier reset, and rule 1 cannot pull him back because B is under both limits. If B were at weekly 70 resetting in 10 h, the strict drain refuses (70 > 49) and overflow fails (A 30 < 50), so he stays. That is correct: a drain that ignored the weekly limit would go A to B, then rule 1 on B (70 >= 50) would find A eligible after 300 s and go back, then the drain again, a switch every 300 s. With overflow: A at 40/60 (strict fired on weekly, so no strict drain), B at 10/85 resetting in 10 h, C at weekly 70 resetting in 3 days. Overflow holds; under relaxed A is below both 90 limits, so nothing counts as reached and the relaxed drain moves him to B. From B: strict fires but has no target; relaxed has no trigger; a drain needs a reset earlier than B's, so he stays. At B weekly 90, the relaxed threshold rule picks C (3 days) before A (4 days). A is never a strict target from B (60 > 49), and drains always go to a strictly earlier reset, so they terminate. His own example (95% used) is not a drain target at 90 in any mode (ceiling 89), the same as 1.9.

(d) No-subscription active account. The strict no-subscription rule needs session <= 89 and weekly <= 49. B at 10/70 and C at 20/80 give strict nil; overflow holds (the active account is exempt and B and C are past their weekly limits); relaxed moves him to B with no cooldown. From B, A has no subscription, so it is never a target and there is no return. Rule 9 as written fails if D is at 95/30 or has no weekly reading: overflow fails and he stays on an account that cannot be used at all. Under the fix, overflow holds whenever strict is nil.

(e) Fable (watched; follows the weekly limit). A at 40/30 with Fable 95, B at 10/70 with Fable 20. Strict: the windows do not fire, Fable fires (95 >= 50), B fails rule 3 (70 > 49), so strict is nil; rule 9 as written stays (A 30 < 50), and so does the fix (a Fable-only trigger does not count). Staying is correct. A relaxed Fable move A to B would be undone: rule 1 on B (70 >= 50) finds A eligible on the windows (40 <= 89, 30 <= 49), and A's Fable trigger would fire again, a ping-pong. With A at weekly 60 (overflow holds), the relaxed Fable trigger needs Fable >= 90. At Fable 55 he stays; at Fable 92 he moves to B if B is at Fable, session and weekly <= 89. A (weekly 60) is never a strict target from B. Under relaxed, keepsFable uses ceiling(90, 1) = 89.

(f) Manual only. A Manual only candidate has rule (0, 0); max(0, 0) = 0 and ceiling is nil, so it is never a target and is correctly left out of the overflow test. A Manual only active account leaves at the defaults (90, 50); relaxed raises defaults.weekly to 90, and the account is never drained (AutoSwitchEngine.swift:336). Rule 9 as written strands it at session 90 or more whenever weekly < 50 (the same as Trace 2); the fix moves it. It never comes back, because Manual only is never a target.

(g) A candidate with no weekly reading. If its session is 89 or less, rule 3 makes it strictly eligible and strict is not nil. Otherwise it is not a target in either mode, so it can only block overflow. Example as written: A at 95/70, B at 10/60, and C whose week reset since its last sample (both windows dropped). He is stranded until C's round-robin turn (the active account plus one other per cycle, recon usage.md:510), or longer if C is parked. Under the fix C blocks nothing, and if C then reads weekly 0, strict moves him to it next cycle, a forward move with no return.

(h) Overrides with weekly above session. P has session 70 and weekly 95, so max(95, 70) = 95 and relaxed == strict for P, which is correct. But as a candidate at 75/60, P is under its weekly ceiling of 94 and has no session room, so overflow never holds for anyone while P's week is below 95%. As the active account at 70/40, P never overflows either (40 < 95), so he is stranded while accounts on the defaults have session room and weekly at 89 or less. The fix handles both.

Cooldown and verification: every return shown above needs a window reset or the target used up to its own limit, never just the 300 s passing. If every target of a strict plan fails verification, he stays this cycle; the fresh readings then make strict nil, and relaxed acts one refresh later. That is acceptable.

Verdict on rule 9 as written: it never ping-pongs, and it keeps 1.9 behaviour when the limits are equal. But it leaves the user at 100% of a session in cases (b) Trace 2 and 2b, (d), (f), (g) and (h). The one-clause fix in new finding 1 removes all of those and keeps every no-ping-pong property, including after the cooldown.
